messages.content: Can you help me find public libraries in New York, NY that have a Reading Room and Fiction section, and then in Los Angeles, CA that offer Wi-Fi and have a Children Section, and finally in Chicago, IL that have a Cafe and a Reading Room?

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function multiple times with different parameters. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location (string) and facilities (one of the listed options). But facilities parameter seems to accept only one value? It says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That suggests it can be an array? Actually the type shows union of string or array? It says "Cafe"[] meaning array of strings? Might be mis-specified. We need to pass facilities as array? The description: "Facilities and sections in public library." So likely we pass an array of desired facilities. We'll pass array of strings.

Thus we need three calls:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We'll call function thrice.
